correctness.rationale: The proof is genuinely all-dimensional for every full-dimensional convex K, interior z and tau>0, not a numerical extrapolation. With a_z=h_K-<z,u>, the perspective psi(a,b)=a log cosh(b/(2a)) is jointly convex, so integrating Jensen gives Phi_zt((1-t)y0+t y1)<= (1-t)Phi_z0(y0)+t Phi_z1(y1) and Minkowski inclusion. For strict root-volume concavity, equality would force centered endpoint convex bodies to be homothetic T_z1=s T_z0; generic boundary y has <y,u> nonzero for S_K-almost every normal, so equality of the perspective integrand forces a_z1=s a_z0 almost everywhere. The identity integral a_z dS_K=d Vol(K) gives s=1; spanning support normals imply z1=z0, contradiction. Pairing opposite normals proves central-origin maximality and uniqueness; simplex vertex-permutation orbit averaging proves centroid uniqueness. Taylor logcosh at y=0 gives Phi=1/8 y^T M_z y+O_z(|y|^4) and the correct sqrt(8 tau) ellipsoid limit. The inequality |r|-log 2 <= logcosh r <= |r| yields the uniform polar projection containment including all interior z. Positive definiteness, d>=2, fixed tau, and no C3 claim for polytope covariograms are explicit. The verified source numerical program illustrates planar cases but does not establish this proof.
